title: API gateway: enforce data residency at request admission (pre-model) + standardized errors
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Implement request admission checks in the Hosted API gateway so that data residency policies (pinned_region/allowed_regions) are enforced before any model execution or downstream side effects occur. When a request violates residency, return standardized HTTP status + machine-readable error code + actionable remediation guidance. The gateway should also attach decision context tags for downstream metrics/audit pipelines.

Scope (this ticket):
- Gateway middleware/hook runs early in request lifecycle (before authz -> routing -> model runtime invocation).
- Determine request region intent and target region (based on endpoint/host + router selection input).
- Call Policy Evaluator service to resolve effective residency policy for org/project/workspace and produce allow/deny.
- Enforce deny with standardized error payload.
- Attach request context tags/headers for downstream services (router/telemetry) to avoid double evaluation.
- Feature-flagged rollout and canary gating.

Non-scope (tracked elsewhere):
- Smart routing changes to avoid cross-region fallback (ENG-2843).
- Audit event emission + SIEM mapping (ENG-2844) beyond minimal context tags.
- Downstream storage enforcement (separate PR/ticket).

References:
- Confluence design spec: design-spec-region-pinning-and-enforcement
- ADR-043: residency enforcement at gateway
- API standard: error-codes-data-residency
acceptance_criteria: Residency check executes before any model execution (verified via tracing span ordering and e2e test that model is not invoked on deny).
If org/project/workspace has pinned_region set and request targets a different region, gateway responds with a 403 and error_code=RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH.
If org has allowed_regions configured and request targets outside the allowlist, gateway responds with a 403 and error_code=RESIDENCY_REGION_NOT_ALLOWED.
Error responses include remediation text: correct base URL/region, where to update Console settings, and docs link.
When residency enforcement is enabled, cross-region fallback is not silently triggered from the gateway (gateway must not rewrite region; router handles capacity decisions per ENG-2843).

Policy evaluator failures: if residency is enabled for the org, fail closed with 503 and error_code=RESIDENCY_POLICY_EVALUATION_FAILED; if residency is not enabled, proceed (no behavioral change for non-enterprise orgs).
Gateway attaches request context fields used by telemetry/audit: residency_decision (allow|deny), evaluated_region, request_region, policy_id/version, and decision_reason (enum).
All logic gated behind feature flag residency_enforcement_gateway_v1 with org allowlist for canary.
Unit tests cover: pinned mismatch, allowlist deny, evaluator timeout, evaluator 5xx, evaluator stale cache header behavior, and no-policy path.
Integration test: pinned EU org hitting US endpoint returns deny + standardized error payload and does not create router/model spans.
implementation_notes: Region derivation: primary signal is the API base host (e.g., api.eu-west.redwood.ai vs api.us-east.redwood.ai). Secondary signal (optional) is SDK-provided region hint header; if the hint conflicts with host-derived region, treat as mismatch and surface explicit remediation (avoid silent override).

Effective policy lookup order: workspace overrides project overrides org. If multiple present, most specific wins. Validation is handled in ENG-2841; gateway assumes stored policies are valid but must handle 'policy_not_found' gracefully.
Policy evaluator call: include org_id, project_id, workspace_id, request_region, product_surface=hosted|dedicated. Expect response: decision, reason, effective_region, policy_version.

Timeout budget: keep P99 overhead <= 5ms in-region. Use short timeout (e.g., 15-25ms) with local cache fallback only when residency is NOT enabled; otherwise fail closed on timeout to avoid residency bypass.
Tracing: create span residency.check at gateway; add attributes residency.decision, residency.request_region, residency.effective_region, residency.reason.

Error payload must follow API standards doc; include fields: error_code, message, request_id, docs_url, remediation_steps (string). (Note: remediation_steps is a string in JSON payload; SDKs will format.)
Do not log customer prompts/completions on deny paths; log only metadata required for debugging (request_id, org_id, region fields, error_code).
rollout_plan:
1) Land behind feature flag residency_enforcement_gateway_v1 (default off).
2) Enable for staging + internal dogfood orgs; validate metrics and tracing tags.
3) Canary cohort (5-10 enterprise pilot orgs) coordinated via PM-482; monitor 403 rate, policy evaluator error rate, and latency impact.
4) Expand to all enterprise orgs once ENG-2843 is live (routing behavior must be deterministic).
5) Document support playbook entry for new errors and common misconfigurations.
testing_plan: Unit tests in gateway middleware package for policy evaluation and error mapping. Add e2e test in integration suite: configure org pinned_region=eu-west, send request to us-east base URL, assert 403 + RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH + no model invocation. Load test on staging to confirm overhead within budget at P95/P99.
open_questions: Should RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH be 403 vs 409? Current API standards doc indicates 403; confirm with Brian Murphy before GA.
Do we want a distinct error for 'SDK region hint mismatches host region' vs treat as RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH with extra remediation copy?
Do we include the evaluated pinned region in the response? (Helpful for debugging, but confirm with Security on information disclosure policy.)
comments: 2025-01-16 (Amara Diallo): Drafted middleware skeleton in gateway. Hook point is pre-router dispatch, after authn but before request body parsing for streaming routes. Need to confirm we can derive region from host reliably for private domains (CNAME).

2025-01-20 (Brian Murphy): Error contract guidance: keep machine-readable error_code stable; message can be more verbose. Include docs_url and a single remediation_steps string; SDKs can surface it. Prefer 403 for policy denies; 503 for evaluator failures when enforcement enabled.

2025-01-23 (Jordan Lee): Policy evaluator response should include decision_reason enum. Please avoid embedding raw policy JSON into gateway logs. Cache key should be (org, project, workspace, request_region) with short TTL; but for enforcement-enabled orgs, failing closed is better than cache-based guess.

2025-01-28 (Amara Diallo): Implemented host-based region derivation with fallback to header x-redwood-client-region for SDK hint. If hint conflicts with host-derived region, deny with RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and remediation pointing to base URL update.

2025-02-03 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE: ensure we emit a counter for denies by error_code and region (even if audit events come later). Also add an explicit metric for evaluator timeouts to detect canary regressions quickly.

2025-02-06 (Amara Diallo): PR up (pr_18435). Added residency.check span and request context tags forwarded to router via internal headers. Still need final sign-off on failing closed behavior for evaluator 5xx when enforcement enabled; currently implemented as fail closed with RESIDENCY_POLICY_EVALUATION_FAILED.
